_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: A failed save keeps the favicon emoji picker open with the error. The server's favicon emoji is 🐙, and its first save fails with "Failed to set favicon emoji: disk on fire". "The picker" is the dialog whose accessible name is "Favicon emoji"; "the favicon" is the element link[rel="icon"]. Call "puts" lists, as a JSON array, the emojis the page has asked the server to save. To "open the picker": press_key "k" with modifiers "Control" (on whatever has focus); fill ".command-palette-input" with "favicon emoji"; click the first ".command-palette-item"; then the picker should be visible. "The search box" is the picker's input[type=search]; it sits inside the emoji-picker element's shadow root, which CSS selectors cannot reach, so pick it as the element with role "combobox" and accessible name exactly "Search" (exact), with "within" the picker. An "option" is an element with role "option" inside the picker. To "type" text means a type step, with no click first: the keys go to whatever has focus. Perform the steps in order. 1. Navigate to /new. 2. [data-testid="message-input"] should be visible. 3. Open the picker. 4. The search box must have focus. 5. Type "cactus". 6. Click the option whose accessible name contains "cactus". 7. The picker's own alert should have text containing "disk on fire": the element with role "alert" picked with "within" the picker ({"role": "dialog", "name": "Favicon emoji"}), since the page has alerts of its own outside it. 8. The favicon's href attribute must be exactly {{OCTOPUS}}. 9. Click the option whose accessible name contains "cactus" again. 10. The picker should become hidden. 11. The favicon's href must be exactly {{CACTUS}}. 12. Open the picker again. 13. The search box must have focus. 14. Press Escape. 15. The picker should become hidden.
